newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Dell sees PC growth up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Dell sees PC growth up 20 pct.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp chairman and chief executive officer Michael Dell said on Tuesday he expected demand for personal computers to grow at a rate near 20 percent in 1997.
He told Reuters that lower prices and new computer chips would be the driving force behind the escalating market for new PCs.
"Over a multi-year period I would put (growth) in the 15-20 percent band. I actually think next year I'd put it closer to 20 percent than 15 percent," Dell said.

"I think you still have this afterglow of the reduction in costs of semiconductors, particularly DRAM, which is driving a huge replacement and new placement cycle because PCs are more cost effective," he said.
Plus, Dell said, "Intel has one of the most dynamic roadmaps they've ever had next year...all these new chips are coming."
He said he expected Dell to benefit from the introduction of the new products because of its policy of selling directly to customers instead of going through resellers.
"In periods of more rapid product transition, the direct model has been able to take advantage of that," he said.

The computer firm said on Tuesday it earned $145 million on revenues of $2.02 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 1997. Dell would not talk about future earnings, but said the company sought to expand its market share in various segments.
"We've done well, but we still have a long, long way to go and lots of opportunity ahead of us. We see tremendous opportunities in growing our share of the desktop and notebook space," he said.
